thread:
Maya P.: Heads-up — Datadog asked for a compact demo bundle we can ship with the marketplace tile: traces + infra + a GPU health dashboard. Want to sync on what the collector config should recommend for Dedicated/Private installs.

Chris L.: Sounds good. Do they want OTLP directly to Datadog or via agent?

Maya P.: They prefer OTLP to our sidecar in Private, and direct OTLP -> Datadog ingestion for Hosted. For Dedicated we should support both but default to sidecar for easier firewall policies.

Evan R.: For GPU nodes we need to include MIG/SM telemetry + per-container GPU mem usage. Datadog has a GPU integration, but we should supply a node_exporter + nvidia-smi scraper config in the pack.

Chris L.: Agreed. I sketched an example collector snippet earlier — keeps batching low to avoid high tail latency on small inference requests. Paste: ```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      http:
      grpc:
processors:
  batch:
    timeout: 200ms
    send_batch_size: 100
exporters:
  datadog:
    api:
      key: ${DD_API_KEY}
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch]
      exporters: [datadog]
```

Maya P.: Nice. Can we add a short note about sampling for reranker-heavy workloads? We should recommend tail-based sampling for long-running chains and a low head_sample_rate for short prompts.

Evan R.: Yep — we'll include a template: tail-sampling rule for >=50 tokens or latency > 500ms. Also include a small Prometheus exporter for KV cache hit/miss per model so customers can tune caching.

Chris L.: For the marketplace tile we want a single-click "install observability pack" that drops: otel-collector yaml (with placeholders), dashboards (Datadog JSON) and a tiny runbook. I can wire up the packaging, but need final dashboard widgets list.

Maya P.: Dashboard should include: 1) end-to-end trace latency histograms (per-model), 2) GPU utilization + MIG slices, 3) KV cache hit rate, 4) batching queue depth over time, 5) error rates + fallback counts (model variant fallbacks). Keep it under 8 widgets so tile stays compact.

Evan R.: I'll create the dashboard JSON and point to sample metrics (we'll use prefix redwood.*). ETA tomorrow EOD.

Chris L.: I'll add an entry in the marketplace README and a sample CLI snippet to deploy the pack. Also add a note for SIs: if they're deploying for customers with strict egress, use the sidecar + datadog-forwarder pattern.

Maya P.: Action items: Evan — dashboard JSON + KV exporter snippet (owner: @Evan R.). Chris — pack manifest + install README + one-click metadata (owner: @Chris L.). Maya — coordinate Datadog partner PM for a joint announcement timeline and a short demo checklist (owner: @Maya P.).

deploy-bot: Deployment note: marketplace-pack branch created: feature/obs-pack-1851 (link: https://git.internal/redwood/marketplace/compare/feature/obs-pack-1851) :white_check_mark:

Chris L.: Quick question — should we include sample traces (synthetic) for the demo to show fallbacks? That helps SIs run the demo offline.

Maya P.: Yes, include a small generator script that emits a few request patterns: short prompt, long chain, reranker + fallback. Put it under /examples/obs/trace-generator. Keep it ~20 lines.

Evan R.: I'll add the generator and a tiny notebook that loads the dashboard locally via Datadog API so partners can preview before pushing to marketplace.

Chris L.: Perfect. I'll ping legal about the co-marketing blurb once we have the pack content.

Maya P.: Thanks team — going to sync with Datadog PM at 10am PT tomorrow. If anything blocks owners, flag here. :rocket:
